# `Q-1-18` — Unknown Property

> A YAML object has a property the schema does not recognize.

## What this means

Some schemas restrict which properties an object may have, in
addition to which are required (`Q-1-10`). Schemas of this kind
are called *closed*: any property name outside the known set is an
error. This is in contrast to *open* schemas, which silently
accept extra properties.

When you place a property name a closed schema does not know, this
error fires. The terminal message names the unknown property and
the object path where it appeared.

## Why this happens

The most common causes:

- **A typo.** What you intended as a recognized property name
  landed under a misspelling. The schema does not see the intended
  property, and the typo looks like an unknown property.
- **A renamed property.** Quarto sometimes renames properties
  between versions. A configuration that worked in an older
  version may contain a name the current schema no longer accepts.
- **A property that belongs to a different block.** Nesting a key
  under the wrong parent in `_quarto.yml` (for example, a
  format-specific key directly under `project:`).

## How to fix

Check the spelling of the property name first; YAML keys are
case-sensitive. If the spelling is right, consult the documentation
for the configuration block — the property may have been renamed,
or it may belong in a sibling block.

If the property is genuinely needed and the schema rejects it, the
schema may be wrong for your case; raise it as an issue with the
Quarto project, naming the property and the block where you wanted
to set it.

## Related

- [`Q-1-10`](Q-1-10.qmd) — missing required property: the schema requires a
  property and your object does not have it.
- [`Q-1-16`](Q-1-16.qmd) — object property count: the property names are all
  valid, but the *count* is wrong.
